'''Otto Grün''' was a German [[mathematician]]. He was known primarily for his work in the theory of [[finite groups]], which have often been praised for being foundational to further developments in the field.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Roquette |first=P. |date=2005 |title=From FLT to Finite Groups The remarkable career of Otto Grün |journal=Sematic Scholar|s2cid=17309465 }}</ref> He was born on June 26, 1888, in [[Berlin]].<ref name="roq4">{{Harvnb|Roquette|2012|page=4}}</ref> He obtained his Ph.D. from [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] in 1948 under the advisory of Hermann Ludwig Schmid.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Otto Grün - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=30022 |access-date=2023-12-21 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref> He died in October 1974 on or before the 10th.<ref name="roq38">{{Harvnb|Roquette|2012|page=38}}</ref>
